boundaries.note: Championship: top 2 automatic, 3rd-8th play off for the 3rd place. Premier League: bottom 3 relegated.
League One: top 2 automatic, 3rd-6th play off for the 3rd place. Championship: bottom 3 relegated.
League Two: top 3 automatic, 4th-7th play off for the 4th place. League One: bottom 4 relegated.
National League: champion + 2nd-7th play-off winner. League Two: bottom 2 relegated into the single national division.

Each level-6 division sends its champion plus one 2nd-7th play-off winner (4 up in total). The National League's bottom 4 are split between North and South by geography, and clubs are transferred between the two divisions to balance numbers.

notes: All sizes, levels and round counts match our rows; nothing to correct. Everything is a single table, double round-robin (20 clubs = 38 rounds, 24 clubs = 46). The one 2026-27 rule change that matters: the Championship play-off went from 4 to 6 clubs (3rd-8th), so 3 of the 3 promotion places are still 2 automatic + 1 play-off. Promotion anywhere in the pyramid is conditional on ground grading/financial criteria, not modelled here. Level 6 is not a floor: each division relegates its bottom 4 to level 7 (Northern Premier, Southern, Isthmian), which is outside our dataset, hence closed_down=false everywhere. Cups and European qualification deliberately excluded.
